abstract: Can one find every small starting value whose Collatz orbit visits a given integer's trajectory before that trajectory first falls below its start? For an original $n\in[X,2X)$ the visitor pool is $1\le a\le\lfloor X/R\rfloor$, and a visitor may take any finite number of steps. We give a deterministic algorithm that lists the visitors and their first contact dates on both the shortcut and ordinary maps. For each fixed integer $p\ge1$, at most $O_p(X/[R^2(1+\ln R)^p])$ originals can have an incomplete answer. The algorithm generates $O_p((1+\ln R)^{p+7})$ inverse nodes per original. It discards an inverse path when its multiplicative gain falls too far below its previous maximum. This places the retained integer sources in short intervals, and a martingale inequality bounds the mass of discarded paths. For odd multiples of three, a second algorithm finds one visitor below $n/R$ at the original's first step, using $O((1+\ln R)^5)$ nodes. It succeeds on $(32\kappa_G/4095+o(1))X/R^2$ originals, a fraction tending to one among all originals admitting such a visitor. Here $\kappa_G$ is the maximum inverse gain tail constant. Both estimates hold as $R\to\infty$ with $R\le X^\epsilon$ for sufficiently small absolute $\epsilon>0$. The supplement checks both clocks against finite orbit enumerations. Finally, if only successive low binary and ternary digits are available and $\ln R=o(\ln X)$, every correct certificate of absence at an individual original requires $\Omega(\ln X)$ digits.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Finding remote Collatz visitors before first descent
